subject: Latency & throughput concordance — dedicated capacity audit and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@streamline.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: performance targets & pilot scope

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on asks and constraints before you produce the pilot matrix: 

- Business SLOs we need validated:
  • End-to-end p95 latency (non-streaming responses): <= 350 ms for median-length responses (~150 tokens).
  • Streaming token latency (time from model token to client): <= 60 ms for p95.
  • Sustained throughput target: 120 requests/sec average during business hours, with 3x burst headroom (360 RPS) for short spikes.
  • Typical response size: 120–220 tokens; average ~180 tokens.
  • Concurrent active sessions: steady 40, peak 80 for 2–3 minute windows.

- Workloads: mixture of short-turn instruction (low latency) and multi-turn assistants (streaming). KV cache reuse expected for ~60% of requests.

- Security: we’ll need SOC2 evidence for the pilot and an IP/PII handling addendum (ops@streamline.ai will send the questionnaire).

Please surface recommended GPU profiles (H100 / A100 / A10G or similar), expected reserved throughput per GPU (tokens/sec and requests/sec for our average response size), and a 2-week pilot plan that proves the SLOs while keeping costs visible.

Attached: preliminary traffic sample + a small csv of request timestamps.

Thanks — Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Platform | StreamlineAI

Attachments referenced: streamline_throughput_matrix.csv

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: performance targets & pilot scope

Maya — thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned on the ask. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) We’ll run a quick capacity audit mapping your traffic sample to per-GPU throughput and concurrency targets.
2) Deliver a short GPU recommendation memo (H100 / A100 / A10G tradeoffs + cost signals) with expected p95/p99 velocities for your average payload.
3) Propose a 2-week dedicated pilot: 1 week smoke + tuning, 1 week sustained run to validate SLOs and collect traces/metrics.

We’ll include a runbook (pilot-runbook.md) that lists test harness commands, required sample traces from your side, and acceptance criteria (SLOs met for 95% of traffic windows; no more than two p99 excursions).

Can you confirm ops@streamline.ai will share the SOC2 questionnaire and a sample spike day (we need a CSV with 1s granularity if possible)? Also what are your preferred windows for the pilot (PST business hours preferred on our side)?

I’ll loop in Karthik with the GPU sizing details shortly.

— Priyom
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya@streamline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-18T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance targets & pilot scope — GPU & throughput notes

Hi team — technical summary and high-level numbers to shape the pilot. These are conservative estimates for an autoregressive 13B-ish model (float16 / q4_0 style quant); we’ll refine after a small microbench with your exact prompt shapes.

- Short summary (per-GPU sustained estimates, avg response ~180 tokens):
  • NVIDIA H100 80GB (best-lowest latency, highest single-stream perf): ~3200 tokens/sec sustained when optimized for streaming; translates to ~17–22 requests/sec at avg 180 tokens (single-stream). With batching (concurrent requests coalesced) we can push higher throughput but will see tail latency tradeoffs.
  • NVIDIA A100 80GB (balanced): ~1800–2200 tokens/sec sustained; ~10–12 requests/sec for 180-token responses. Better cost/$ for sustained workloads.
  • NVIDIA A10G (cost-optimized): ~700–1000 tokens/sec; ~3–5 requests/sec for the same response size — good for non-low-latency, throughput-focused tasks.

- Reserved throughput sizing (recommended for your profile):
  • Baseline steady (120 RPS avg): at 180 tokens/resp -> ~21,600 tokens/sec.
  • With H100 only: ~7–8 GPUs reserved (7*3200 = 22,400 tokens/sec) to meet steady-state with small headroom.
  • With mixed pool (2x H100 + 6x A100): peak handling & cost balance — H100s handle low-latency streaming sessions while A100s absorb background batchy throughput.
  • With A100-only: ~11–12 A100s to reach steady tokens/sec.

- Concurrency & batching guidance:
  • Target continuous batching window of 8–12 ms for throughput-sensitive paths. Keep per-request coalescing small for streaming flows to avoid per-token tail latency.
  • Use prefix/KV cache aggressively — with ~60% cache reuse your effective tokens/sec requirement drops ~35–40%. We’ll validate this against your sample.

- Acceptance criteria we’ll validate in pilot:
  • End-to-end p95 non-streaming latency <= 350 ms for >= 95% of 1-hour windows over the 1-week sustained run.
  • Streaming p95 per-token <= 60 ms under steady traffic.
  • No more than 2 p99 violations outside maintenance windows during the sustained run.

I’m attaching a quick csv with the throughput mapping and a one-page GPU recommendation PDF. We’ll kick an internal microbench with your sample to replace these estimates with measured numbers.

— Karthik
Applied ML / Inference Optimization | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: streamline_throughput_matrix.csv, redwood_gpu_reco_summary.pdf
